advisory.finding: actions/cache is referenced with a floating major-version tag `@v6` inside the local composite action, not pinned to a commit SHA, unlike every other third-party action in the workflows (e.g. actions/setup-python@5fda3b95...). The release-pin test only checks workflow files and explicitly skips `./` paths, so this transitive action reference is unpinned and unguarded.
merged_from: The committed SHA256 checksums in action.yml are pinned to a specific uv release's artifacts, but the uv version is read dynamically from pyproject.toml [tool.uv] required-version. Nothing ties the checksum set to the version, so bumping required-version without updating the six checksums produces a runtime checksum-mismatch outage rather than a clear consistency error, and check_uv_pin.py cannot detect the mismatch because it never compares checksums to the pinned version.

The provenance of the six committed SHA256 digests is not documented — there is no record of how they were obtained (e.g. from astral-sh/uv release attestations or the published checksums file), so a reviewer cannot verify the pinned artifact hashes are authentic rather than attacker-supplied.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `uses: actions/cache@v6` with a SHA-pinned reference, e.g. `uses: actions/cache@<40-char-sha>  # v6.x`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `uv --version` succeeded (check `$LASTEXITCODE`/throw on non-zero) before printing the 'Successfully installed uv' liveness anchor.
evidence: `& $installedUv --version`
`Write-Host "Successfully installed uv $version from $asset"`
action.yml:96-98 — the `--version` call's `$LASTEXITCODE` is never inspected before printing the success anchor
Ticket AC-1: 'the anchor is asserted FIRST — a zero-match grep alone is also produced by an empty log or a skipped step' — the anchor is meant to prove liveness
dropped.finding: The `& $installedUv --version` invocation is used as the install-liveness signal, but its exit status is never checked. In PowerShell a native command exiting non-zero does not raise under `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` (that requires `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference`), so a corrupt/incompatible uv binary still falls through to `Write-Host "Successfully installed uv $version..."`. The acceptance anchor that CI greps for liveness (AC-1) can therefore print even when uv is not actually runnable.
dropped.suggested_fix: After `& $installedUv --version`, add `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "uv --version failed with exit $LASTEXITCODE" }` so the success anchor only prints when uv actually runs.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the uv Windows zip lays uv.exe under a `uv-<target>/` dir; if it can sit at the archive root, drop or relax the `*$target*` FullName filter so the Windows executable is still found.
evidence: `$uv = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $extractDir -Recurse -File -Filter $uvExecutable | Where-Object { $_.FullName -like "*$target*" } | Select-Object -First 1`
`if (-not $uv) { throw "Could not find $uvExecutable in $asset" }`

ABSENCE: the uv Windows zip's internal directory layout cannot be verified from this repo; the `*$target*` FullName constraint fails if uv.exe sits at the zip root rather than under a `uv-<target>/` folder
dropped.finding: The executable-locating filter `Where-Object { $_.FullName -like "*$target*" }` requires the extracted uv/uv.exe path to contain the target triple (e.g. `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`). uv's Linux/macOS tarballs extract into a `uv-<target>/` directory (matches), but if the Windows `.zip` lays `uv.exe` at the archive root (no target-named subdir), the filter matches nothing and the step throws `Could not find uv.exe`. The Windows install path may be broken depending on the release archive layout.
dropped.suggested_fix: Take the first matching executable without the target-path constraint, or fall back to a target-agnostic search when the constrained search yields nothing.
